Basic Check: Check if the monitor is turned on.
Check the HDMI, DisplayPort or USB-C cable.
Check the correct input source on the monitor.
Press Win + P and check the display mode.
Open Settings > System > Display and check if Windows detects the monitor.
1. No image or No Signal: The monitor is on, but it is not receiving a video signal.
Check the video cable on both ends.
Select the correct input source, for example HDMI or DisplayPort.
Try another cable or video port.
Test the monitor with another computer.
2. Second monitor is not detected: Windows can see only one monitor.
Check the cable and the monitor power.
Press Win + P and select Extend.
Use Detect if the second monitor is missing.
Check the graphics driver in Device Manager.
3. Wrong resolution or scale: Text, icons or the picture look too large, too small or blurry.
Set Display resolution to the Recommended value.
Use the monitor's native resolution when possible.
4. Screen is flickering: The image flashes, blinks or is not stable.
Press Win + Ctrl + Shift + B to restart the graphics driver.
Check the graphics driver in Device Manager.
5. Wrong display mode: The picture is shown on the wrong screen or the second monitor is not used correctly.
Choose PC screen only, Duplicate, Extend or Second screen only.
Use Extend when you want two separate desktop areas.
6. Screen has strange colors or is black: The monitor may be working correctly, but Windows accessibility settings can change the colors.
Turn off any display accessibility option that was enabled by mistake.
